title: Basophils

review.note: Drafted from the source below; not yet reviewed by a medical professional.

measures: Basophils are a type of white blood cell that releases enzymes during allergic reactions and asthma. A blood differential measures the amount or percentage of basophils.
context: A blood differential is often part of a routine checkup. An out-of-range result does not always mean a condition that needs care, and your provider considers your symptoms, history, and other blood tests.
aboveRange: Can be associated with autoimmune or inflammatory conditions
Can be associated with leukemia or Hodgkin disease
belowRange: Can be associated with bone marrow conditions
Chemotherapy or certain medicines such as antibiotics
Physical injury, extreme stress, smoking, or alcohol use may also affect results
nextStep: Discuss this result with your doctor.
